documents.title: Monitoring note, hearing 1 (2 June 2025)
documents.text:
TRIAL MONITORING NOTE
Case: Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn (Mirevo District Court, Criminal Chamber, case no. MDC-2025-0147)
Hearing: 1
Hearing date: 2 June 2025
Monitor: R.T.

The trial opened on 2 June 2025 at 10:05 before Presiding Judge Ilena Varda, sitting with two lay assessors. About twenty members of the public and three journalists attended, and the courtroom doors remained open.

Mr. Venn was present in the courtroom throughout the hearing, seated in a glass dock. Defence counsel Lena Brask, whom Mr. Venn had retained himself, was present and sat beside the dock.

According to the case file and to his counsel, Mr. Venn's first language is Ostric; he grew up in the Ostric-speaking north of the country.

The presiding judge read out the charge under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code. Mr. Venn confirmed that he had received the indictment on 4 March 2025.

Ms. Brask told the court that she had received the 900-page case file only three days before this hearing and asked for an adjournment of two weeks to prepare the defence. The presiding judge refused the request and ordered the trial to continue.

Ms. Brask reminded the court that Mr. Venn had been arrested at his home before dawn on 14 February 2025 and was questioned by police for two days. She stated that she was first able to meet Mr. Venn on 21 February 2025, a week after his arrest.

The presiding judge informed Mr. Venn that he had the right to remain silent. Mr. Venn chose to make a statement, in which he denied the charge and said that his articles were based on documents given to him by employees of the Ministry of Water.

The hearing ended at 13:40.

documents.title: Monitoring note, hearing 2 (16 June 2025)
documents.text:
TRIAL MONITORING NOTE
Case: Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn (Mirevo District Court, Criminal Chamber, case no. MDC-2025-0147)
Hearing: 2
Hearing date: 16 June 2025
Monitor: R.T.

The hearing began at 10:10 before Presiding Judge Ilena Varda. The courtroom was open to the public.

Mr. Venn was present in the dock for the whole hearing. Defence counsel Lena Brask was present and represented him.

Two officials of the Ministry of Water testified for the prosecution. Both said that the figures in Mr. Venn's articles did not match the audited project accounts. Ms. Brask cross-examined both witnesses about who had prepared the audit.

Defence counsel argued that the messages presented by the prosecution had been extracted from Mr. Venn's mobile telephone, which police seized at his home on 14 February 2025 without a judicial warrant, and asked the court to exclude them as evidence. The prosecutor replied that the seizure was lawful because the telephone was found during the arrest. The presiding judge said that the court would rule on the request later.

The hearing ended at 12:55.

documents.title: Monitoring note, hearing 3 (30 June 2025)
documents.text:
TRIAL MONITORING NOTE
Case: Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn (Mirevo District Court, Criminal Chamber, case no. MDC-2025-0147)
Hearing: 3
Hearing date: 30 June 2025
Monitor: R.T.

The hearing began at 10:00 before Presiding Judge Ilena Varda.

Mr. Venn was present in the dock when the hearing opened. Defence counsel Lena Brask was present.

The presiding judge ruled that the messages taken from Mr. Venn's telephone were admissible, without giving reasons. Ms. Brask's objection was recorded.

At the prosecution's request, the presiding judge ordered the public and journalists to leave the courtroom during the testimony of a police investigator, citing national security. The monitor was also asked to leave and could not observe that part of the hearing.

When the public was readmitted, a second police investigator testified about the analysis of the telephone. Ms. Brask questioned him about how the messages had been extracted.

Defence counsel asked the court to hear two witnesses, both editors at Mirevo Today, who had attended the editorial meeting at which the articles were approved. The presiding judge refused to hear them, without giving reasons.

Defence counsel argued that the first article was published before the amendment to Article 214 entered into force, so that Mr. Venn could not be punished for conduct that was lawful at the time.

The hearing ended at 14:20.

Case: Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn (Mirevo District Court, Criminal Chamber, case no. MDC-2025-0147)
Hearing: 4
Hearing date: 14 July 2025
Monitor: R.T.

The hearing began at 09:30 before Presiding Judge Ilena Varda. The courtroom was open to the public.

documents.title: Indictment (3 March 2025)
documents.text:
OFFICE OF THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR OF MIREVO
INDICTMENT
Case no. MDC-2025-0147
The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn
Mirevo, 3 March 2025

I. THE ACCUSED

Daro Venn, born on 11 May 1987 in Halvar, journalist, residing in Mirevo.

II. PROCEDURAL HISTORY

The accused was arrested at his home in Mirevo in the early morning of 14 February 2025. On 15 February 2025 the accused was brought before the Public Prosecutor, who ordered that he remain in police custody. On 19 February 2025 the accused was brought before Judge Ilena Varda of the Mirevo District Court, who ordered his detention pending trial. On 3 March 2025 the Public Prosecutor filed this indictment with the Mirevo District Court.

III. STATEMENT OF FACTS

Between 9 February and 12 February 2025, the accused published a series of articles on the news portal Mirevo Today alleging that officials of the Ministry of Water had diverted public funds intended for the northern irrigation project. The articles were shared more than 40,000 times within three days and caused public alarm in the northern districts, where residents gathered outside the regional water office on 13 February 2025. The accused knew that the allegations were false, because the Ministry had published the audited project accounts on 2 February 2025, a week before the first article appeared. Messages recovered from the accused's mobile telephone show that he coordinated the timing of the publications with persons abroad in order to maximise their impact. The conduct of the accused was deliberate and was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State.

IV. EVIDENCE

The prosecution relies on the articles published on Mirevo Today, the audited accounts of the northern irrigation project, the testimony of two officials of the Ministry of Water and of two police investigators, and the messages recovered from the accused's mobile telephone.

V. LEGAL QUALIFICATION

Article 214(2) of the Penal Code provides: "Whoever disseminates information that he knows to be false, where such dissemination is likely to cause public alarm, shall be punished by imprisonment of two to six years."

VI. CHARGE

The accused is charged with disseminating false information likely to cause public alarm, an offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code.

The Public Prosecutor requests that the accused be found guilty and sentenced to imprisonment.

(signed) Malik Ferrow, Public Prosecutor of Mirevo

documents.title: Judgment (14 July 2025)
documents.text:
MIREVO DISTRICT COURT, CRIMINAL CHAMBER
JUDGMENT
Case no. MDC-2025-0147
The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn
Delivered on 14 July 2025
Presiding Judge: Ilena Varda
Lay assessors: Oren Valk and Teja Morrow

I. PROCEDURAL HISTORY

The accused was arrested on 14 February 2025 and was brought before this Court on 19 February 2025, which ordered his detention pending trial. His detention was extended on 19 March 2025 and again on 14 May 2025. The indictment was filed on 3 March 2025. The trial opened on 2 June 2025, and the Court held four hearings.

II. THE CHARGE

The accused is charged with disseminating false information likely to cause public alarm, an offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code.

III. SUBMISSIONS OF THE PARTIES

The prosecution argues that the accused knew that the allegations were false and that his conduct was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State. The defence contends that the messages relied on by the prosecution were extracted from a telephone seized without a judicial warrant and must be excluded. The defence further argues that the first article was published before the amendment to Article 214 entered into force.

IV. THE APPLICABLE LAW

Article 214(2) of the Penal Code provides: "Whoever disseminates information that he knows to be false, where such dissemination is likely to cause public alarm, shall be punished by imprisonment of two to six years."

V. ASSESSMENT OF THE COURT

Between 9 February and 12 February 2025, the accused published a series of articles on the news portal Mirevo Today alleging that officials of the Ministry of Water had diverted public funds intended for the northern irrigation project. The articles were shared more than 40,000 times within three days and caused public alarm in the northern districts, where residents gathered outside the regional water office on 13 February 2025. The accused knew that the allegations were false, because the Ministry had published the audited project accounts on 2 February 2025, a week before the first article appeared.

Messages retrieved from the telephone of the accused demonstrate that he arranged when the articles would appear together with individuals outside the country, so as to increase their effect.

The Court has examined the testimony of the two officials of the Ministry of Water, each of whom confirmed that the published figures did not match the audited accounts. The Court considers their testimony credible and consistent.

As to the defence argument that the first article predates the amendment to Article 214, the Court notes that the amendment entered into force on 1 January 2025, while the first article appeared on 9 February 2025. That argument is therefore rejected.

The Court finds that the conduct of the accused was deliberate and was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State.

In determining the sentence, the Court has taken into account that the accused has no previous convictions.

VI. DISPOSITION

For these reasons, the Court finds the accused Daro Venn guilty of the offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code and sentences him to four years' imprisonment. The time spent in pretrial detention since 19 February 2025 shall be deducted from the sentence.

(signed) Ilena Varda, Presiding Judge

documents.text:
MIREVO DISTRICT COURT, CRIMINAL CHAMBER
DETENTION ORDER
Case no. MDC-2025-0147
The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn
Date: 19 February 2025
Judge: Ilena Varda

I. REQUEST

The Public Prosecutor requests that the accused be detained pending trial.

II. APPLICABLE LAW

Article 167(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides: "Detention pending trial may be ordered where there is a reasonable suspicion that the accused committed the offence and a risk that he will flee, interfere with the evidence or commit a further offence."

III. GROUNDS

There is a reasonable suspicion that the accused published articles containing false information about the Ministry of Water that caused public alarm. The accused has relatives in a neighbouring country and travelled there twice in the past year, so there is a risk that he will flee. The accused knows the officials of the Ministry of Water who are expected to testify, and there is a risk that he will seek to influence their statements. The offence carries a penalty of up to six years of imprisonment.

IV. DECISION

The accused shall be detained pending trial until 19 March 2025.

(signed) Ilena Varda

documents.title: Detention extension order (19 March 2025)
documents.text:
MIREVO DISTRICT COURT, CRIMINAL CHAMBER
DETENTION EXTENSION ORDER
Case no. MDC-2025-0147
The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn
Date: 19 March 2025
Judge: Ilena Varda

I. REQUEST

The Public Prosecutor requests that the detention of the accused be extended by two months.

II. APPLICABLE LAW

Article 167(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides: "Detention pending trial may be ordered where there is a reasonable suspicion that the accused committed the offence and a risk that he will flee, interfere with the evidence or commit a further offence."

III. GROUNDS

The accused has relatives in a neighbouring country and travelled there twice in the past year, so there is a risk that he will flee. The forensic examination of the telephone seized from the accused has not yet been completed, and its results are needed to establish when the articles were prepared. Since the first order, two of the officials expected to testify have reported being approached by acquaintances of the accused, which shows that the risk of interference persists. The Court has considered whether house arrest or a duty to report to the police would be sufficient, and finds that neither would prevent such approaches.

IV. DECISION

The detention of the accused is extended until 12 May 2025.

(signed) Ilena Varda

The defence contends that the messages relied on by the prosecution were extracted from a telephone seized without a judicial warrant and must be excluded.
The defence further argues that the first article was published before the amendment to Article 214 entered into force.
IV. THE APPLICABLE LAW

Article 214(2) of the Penal Code provides: "Whoever disseminates information that he knows to be false, where such dissemination is likely to cause public alarm, shall be punished by imprisonment of two to six years."
V. ASSESSMENT OF THE COURT

Between 9 February and 12 February 2025, the accused published a series of articles on the news portal Mirevo Today alleging that officials of the Ministry of Water had diverted public funds intended for the northern irrigation project.
The articles were shared more than 40,000 times within three days and caused public alarm in the northern districts, where residents gathered outside the regional water office on 13 February 2025.
The accused knew that the allegations were false, because the Ministry had published the audited project accounts on 2 February 2025, a week before the first article appeared.
Messages retrieved from the telephone of the accused demonstrate that he arranged when the articles would appear together with individuals outside the country, so as to increase their effect.
The Court has examined the testimony of the two officials of the Ministry of Water, each of whom confirmed that the published figures did not match the audited accounts.
The Court considers their testimony credible and consistent.

As to the defence argument that the first article predates the amendment to Article 214, the Court notes that the amendment entered into force on 1 January 2025, while the first article appeared on 9 February 2025.
That argument is therefore rejected.
The Court finds that the conduct of the accused was deliberate and was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State.
In determining the sentence, the Court has taken into account that the accused has no previous convictions.
VI. DISPOSITION
For these reasons, the Court finds the accused Daro Venn guilty of the offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code and sentences him to four years' imprisonment.
The time spent in pretrial detention since 19 February 2025 shall be deducted from the sentence.
(signed) Ilena Varda, Presiding Judge

Case no. MDC-2025-0147
The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn
Date: 14 May 2025

The Public Prosecutor requests that the detention of the accused be extended by two months.

Article 167(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides: "Detention pending trial may be ordered where there is a reasonable suspicion that the accused committed the offence and a risk that he will flee, interfere with the evidence or commit a further offence."
The detention of the accused is extended until 14 July 2025.
(signed) Ilena Varda

venn-2025/judgment.txt.whole: MIREVO DISTRICT COURT, CRIMINAL CHAMBER JUDGMENT Case no. MDC-2025-0147 The Republic of Calderra v. Daro Venn Delivered on 14 July 2025 Presiding Judge: Ilena Varda Lay assessors: Oren Valk and Teja Morrow I. PROCEDURAL HISTORY The accused was arrested on 14 February 2025 and was brought before this Court on 19 February 2025, which ordered his detention pending trial.not reasoning His detention was extended on 19 March 2025 and again on 14 May 2025.not reasoning The indictment was filed on 3 March 2025.not reasoning The trial opened on 2 June 2025, and the Court held four hearings.not reasoning II. THE CHARGE The accused is charged with disseminating false information likely to cause public alarm, an offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code.charge recital III. SUBMISSIONS OF THE PARTIES The prosecution argues that the accused knew that the allegations were false and that his conduct was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State.party position The defence contends that the messages relied on by the prosecution were extracted from a telephone seized without a judicial warrant and must be excluded.party position The defence further argues that the first article was published before the amendment to Article 214 entered into force.party position IV. THE APPLICABLE LAW Article 214(2) of the Penal Code provides: "Whoever disseminates information that he knows to be false, where such dissemination is likely to cause public alarm, shall be punished by imprisonment of two to six years."statute quote V. ASSESSMENT OF THE COURT Between 9 February and 12 February 2025, the accused published a series of articles on the news portal Mirevo Today alleging that officials of the Ministry of Water had diverted public funds intended for the northern irrigation project1. The articles were shared more than 40,000 times within three days and caused public alarm in the northern districts, where residents gathered outside the regional water office on 13 February 20252. The accused knew that the allegations were false, because the Ministry had published the audited project accounts on 2 February 2025, a week before the first article appeared3. Messages retrieved from the telephone of the accused demonstrate that he arranged when the articles would appear together with individuals outside the country, so as to increase their effect.4 The Court has examined the testimony of the two officials of the Ministry of Water, each of whom confirmed that the published figures did not match the audited accounts. The Court considers their testimony credible and consistent. As to the defence argument that the first article predates the amendment to Article 214, the Court notes that the amendment entered into force on 1 January 2025, while the first article appeared on 9 February 2025. That argument is therefore rejected. The Court finds that the conduct of the accused was deliberate and was intended to undermine public confidence in the institutions of the State5. In determining the sentence, the Court has taken into account that the accused has no previous convictions. VI. DISPOSITION For these reasons, the Court finds the accused Daro Venn guilty of the offence under Article 214(2) of the Penal Code and sentences him to four years' imprisonment.not reasoning The time spent in pretrial detention since 19 February 2025 shall be deducted from the sentence.not reasoning (signed) Ilena Varda, Presiding Judge

THE ACCUSED Daro Venn, born on 11 May 1987 in Halvar, journalist, residing in Mirevo. II. PROCEDURAL HISTORY The accused was arrested at his home in Mirevo in the early morning of 14 February 2025.
